criteria.evidence: Turn 0: explains the second revision dir is the 'exclude branch' of snap_sync_exclude_paths(), computed on the source, so uat-stray must be absent on pc2 per §6.

Turns 2-3: 'my sandbox has no ssh, no hcloud, no network' / 'There is no ssh client in this environment'; verdict reasoned from ADR-020 measurements and flatpak_sync.py:1711 (though turn 1 initially handed the user commands).
Turn 2/4: 'the runbook is wrong, the tool is right. Not a product bug' — allow-only filter denies nothing so sopwith is still offered and the check correctly returns without aborting.
Diff: §3 check 2 now `printf 'deny *\nallow org.freedesktop.*\n' > /home/testuser/uat.filter` with comment on the deny line.
Turn 5: 'expected — and it's the runbook's framing that's wrong, not the tool', shape question asked in plan() before the registry is read.
Diff §3 preamble: 'The first two end it before any question at all; the third ends it after the one question the /opt scan asks ahead of the review'; no behaviour change made, choice stated.
Diff §4: 'the collateral question `<y>`, the answer reading `remove fortunes-min from pc2, so fortunes is removed as well`'.
Diff §4: 'the repository deletion `<s>`, which apt asks in a second review round of its own — a fresh set of screens after the package ones are confirmed'.

Diff §4/§5: 'hello-world left at install on Install snap packages and then hello's revision change'; §5 'snap_sync asks twice, installs before changes ... Install snap packages comes first and holds hello-world'.

Diff §4/§5: 'io.github.fragglet.sdl_sopwith left at install on Install flatpak applications' placed after snap screens; §5 'flatpak_sync asks one question ... on a row that starts applied' (full ref suffix not spelled out).
Turn 12 justifies 'one application' as pinning a single finding for §6, matches no-terminal default; §6 grep fixed to count one label entry and notes the alternative.
Diff §4: 'one item per screen in path order — /opt/pcsw-uat-app first, answered `<y>` ... and /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor after it, answered `<x>`'.

Turn 15: 'hello auto-refreshed' — snapd refresh paused only during RUN_JOBS (orchestrator.py:77-90), both machines now on the same revision; VMs already established unreachable, check commands supplied.
Turn 15: re-run `ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'sudo snap refresh --revision=<that second revision> hello'`.
Diff §4 new paragraph: 'Before EACH run, snap list hello on both machines; where they agree, put pc2 back with sudo snap refresh --revision=... hello'.
not observable — only .md files changed; no spelling defects visible in the diff.

judge.reason: Every runbook correction the criteria name is present in the replay diff (filter deny line, §3 check-3 ordering, collateral `<y>`, second-round clarification, hello-world and sopwith questions, manual-review order, per-run re-pin) and each divergence received a verdict consistent with the code after the replay disclosed it could not reach the VMs. Doubt remains because turn 1 first handed the user commands before the no-ssh fallback, the sopwith ref is given without its /x86_64/stable suffix, and the codespell run is not observable.
